title: Tracking Charge Dynamics by High Speed and Time Resolved Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
content: Quantifying charge dynamics at the nanoscale is crucial for understanding electronic, ionic, and electrochemical processes in materials and devices—such as batteries, fuel cells, and bioelectronics—and for linking them to macroscopic properties. Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM), with its high spatial resolution (∼10 nm), is a powerful tool for mapping work function differences, as well as surface and electronic potentials at grain boundaries, domain walls, interfaces, and between distinct phases. KPFM also has applications in electrochemical systems, where it can indirectly probe electrochemical potentials through temporal variations in the measured contact potential difference (CPD). However, conventional KPFM is often limited by slow temporal resolution (on the order of minutes), making it challenging to capture dynamic charge phenomena across relevant length and time scales.
